subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Movement for Mental Health and Sustainable Routine
essentialQuestion: How do I keep moving through a year that gives me every reason not to?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of movement and mood: what the evidence supports and what it does not in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe routine design for low-motivation periods using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply the smallest version of a session that still counts in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving social activity, accountability, and isolation; correct it and explain why.
Connect compulsive activity, overtraining, and warning signs with when to seek support beyond movement and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Design a sustainable activity routine with a full version, a minimum version, and a restart procedure, and state the warning signs that would prompt the learner to seek support.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: Every routine element has a low-intensity, seated, short-duration, and at-home version; the minimum version must be achievable on the learner’s worst realistic day.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
